source.note: Full text of ASME BPVC Section II, Part A (Ferrous Material Specifications), Volume 2 — SA-905 - Specification for Steel Wire, Pressure Vessel Winding — as supplied by Daniel Velasquez on 2026-09-07 and extracted from the supplied PDF with marker-pdf. `data` is the extractor's output verbatim — the drop's own `document`, `part`, `figures` and `pages` blocks, with the page-by-page block tree, its HTML, tables and layout coordinates unedited. This file IS the source document, so `transcribed_from` names its own path: it is the artefact under review, not a transcription of one. The volume was supplied as one combined PDF and cut into parts at its own headings, so this file is a page-range slice of a single extraction and its page ids (PDF pages None–None, no printed page numbers on these pages) are the combined document's own, not renumbered from 0. Front matter (cover and title page, contents, list of sections, foreword, statement of policy, personnel, correspondence, summary of changes, cross-referencing) and back matter (back cover) were deleted from the drop before supply and are NOT filed; the drop's `content.json`, `index.json`, `meta.json` and `README.md` are retained beside the kind folders, unfiled, for the same reason. The edition — 2025 Edition (ASME BPVC.II.A-2025), issued 2025-07-01 — is stated on the title page, which this drop no longer carries as a filed cut: it survives only inside the retained `content.json`, so no filed cut of this standard prints its own edition. This cut carries no figure.

ASME SA-905 adds the following "Class 2" column to Table 2 of ASTM A905:
Standard Specification for Steel Wire, Pressure Vessel Winding1

This standard is issued under the fixed designation A905; the number immediately following the designation indicates the year of original adoption or, in the case of revision, the year of last revision. A number in parentheses indicates the year of last reapproval. A superscript epsilon (´) indicates an editorial change since the last revision or reapproval.

1.1 This specification covers requirements for a high strength drawn and cold rolled steel wire in two strength classes, with rectangular cross section, and round mill edge. This wire is intended for prestressed vessel and press frame windings.

1.2 The values stated in either inch-pound units or SI (metric) units are to be regarded separately as standards. Within the text and tables, the SI units are shown in parentheses. The values stated in each system are not exact equivalents. Therefore, each system must be used independent of the other. Combining values from the two systems may result in nonconformance with the specification.

1.3 This international standard was developed in accordance with internationally recognized principles on standardization established in the Decision on Principles for the Development of International Standards, Guides and Recommendations issued by the World Trade Organization Technical Barriers to Trade (TBT) Committee.

2.1 ASTM Standards:2 A370 Test Methods and Definitions for Mechanical Testing of Steel Products A510/A510M Specification for General Requirements for Wire Rods and Coarse Round Wire, Carbon Steel, and Alloy Steel A700 Guide for Packaging, Marking, and Loading Methods for Steel Products for Shipment A751 Test Methods, Practices, and Terminology for Chemical Analysis of Steel Products E309 Practice for Eddy Current Examination of Steel Tubular Products Using Magnetic Saturation
2.2 Federal Standard:3 Fed. Std. No. 123 Marking for Shipment (Civil Agencies)

3.1 It shall be the responsibility of the purchaser to specify all requirements that are necessary for material under this specification. Such requirements may include, but are not limited to, the following:

3.1.1 Quantity (mass), 3.1.2 Name of material, 3.1.3 Dimensions (see Section 7), 3.1.4 Finish (see Section 8), 3.1.5 Packaging (see Section 11), 3.1.6 Cast or heat analysis report (see Section 5), 3.1.7 Number of certification or test reports required (see Section 10), 3.1.8 ASTM designation and year of issue, and 3.1.9 Supplementary requirements, if any.

4.1 The steel shall be produced by any of the following primary processes: (1) basic oxygen, and (2) electric furnace or vacuum induction (VIM). The primary melting may incorporate separate degassing or refining and may be followed by secondary melting by the electrode slag process (ESR) or the vacuum arc remelting process (VAR).
4.1.1 The steel may be ingot cast or continuously cast. 4.2 The finished wire shall be free from detrimental pipe
4.3 The wire shall be cold drawn or cold rolled, or both, to produce the desired mechanical properties and dimensions after subjecting it to the patenting treatment.
4.4 The width to thickness ratio of the wire cross section
5.1 The steel shall conform to the requirements for chemical composition prescribed in Table 1.
1 This specification is under the jurisdiction of ASTM Committee A01 on Steel, Stainless Steel and Related Alloys and is the direct responsibility of Subcommittee A01.03 on Steel Rod and Wire.
Current edition approved Sept. 1, 2019. Published September 2019. Originally approved in 1991. Last previous edition approved in 2017 as A905 – 04 (2017). DOI: 10.1520/A0905-19.

2 For referenced ASTM standards, visit the ASTM website, www.astm.org, or contact ASTM Customer Service at service@astm.org. For Annual Book of ASTM Standards volume information, refer to the standard's Document Summary page on the ASTM website.
3 Available from Standardization Documents Order Desk, DODSSP, Bldg. 4, Section D, 700 Robbins Ave., Philadelphia, PA 19111-5094, https:// quicksearch.dla.mil.

5.2 Heat Analysis—Each heat of steel shall be analyzed to determine the percentage of elements prescribed in Table 1. This analysis shall be made from a test specimen preferably taken during the pouring of the heat. When requested, this shall be reported to the purchaser and shall conform to the requirements of Table 1.

5.3 Product Analysis—An analysis may be made by the purchaser from finished wire representing each heat of steel. The chemical composition thus determined, as to elements required or restricted, shall conform to the product analysis requirements specified in Table 10 of Specification A510/ A510M.
5.4 For referee purposes, Test Methods, Practices, and Terminology A751 shall be used.
6.1.1 Requirements—The material as represented by tension test specimens shall conform to the requirements prescribed in Table 2.
6.1.2 Number of Tests—One test specimen shall be taken from each end of every coil.

6.1.3 Test Method—The tension test shall be made in accordance with Test Methods and Definitions A370, except that the length L for evaluation of the elongation shall be calculated from the following formula:
W = width of the wire, and
The length L shall be used to calculate the permanent elongation. The distance between the gage marks shall be measured to the nearest 0.004 in. (0.1 mm). Determine tensile
properties and permanent elongation as described in Test Methods and Definitions A370.
6.1.4 Retest—If any test specimen exhibits obvious discontinuity, it may be discarded and another specimen substituted.
7.1 The permissible variations in dimensions of the wire shall be as specified in Table 3, unless otherwise specified in the ordering information.
8.1 The wire shall be free of detrimental surface imperfections, tangles and sharp kinks.
8.2 The wire shall conform to the dimensions, tolerances, and finish specified on the order or drawing. Welds are not permitted.
8.3 When required, non-destructive examination shall be carried out in accordance with Supplementary Requirement S1.
8.4 The wire as received shall be smooth and substantially free from rust. No detrimental die marks or scratches may be present.

9.1 The manufacturer shall afford the purchaser's inspector all reasonable facilities to satisfy him that the material is being produced and furnished in accordance with this specification. All tests and inspections may be made at the place of manufacture prior to shipment and shall be so conducted as to not interfere unnecessarily with the operation of the work.
10.1 The manufacturer shall furnish the required number, from the purchase order, of test reports to the purchaser. The following items shall be reported.
10.1.3 Result of test of tensile properties,
10.1.4 Reports of non-destructive tests, if required (S.1), and
10.1.5 ASTM specification number, year of issue and revision letter, if any.
11. Packaging, Marking, and Loading for Shipment
11.1 The coil, reel or spool mass, dimensions, and the method of packaging shall be agreed upon between the manufacturer and purchaser.
11.2 The size of the wire, purchaser's order number, ASTM specification number, and name or mark of the manufacturer shall be marked on a tag securely attached to each coil, reel, or spool of wire.
11.3 Unless otherwise specified in the purchaser's order, packaging, marking, and loading for shipments shall be in accordance with those procedures recommended by Practices A700.
11.4 For Government Procurement—Marking for shipment of material for civil agencies shall be in accordance with Fed. Std. No. 123.

Supplementary requirements to this specification shall only apply to a product specification when specified by the purchaser in his inquiry, contract or order. Details of the supplementary requirements shall be agreed upon in writing between the manufacturer and purchaser.
S1.1 The surface of the wire shall be examined by the eddy current method in accordance with Practice E309. The acceptance criteria shall be mutually agreed upon by the purchaser and manufacturer.
Committee A01 has identified the location of selected changes to this standard since the last issue (A905 – 04 (2017)) that may impact the use of this standard. (Approved Sept. 1, 2019.)
(1) Removed Test Methods E30, MIL-STD-163, and AIAG
(2) Added Test Methods A751 to Referenced Documents. (3) Combined Specifications A510 and A510M into A510/ A510M in Referenced Documents. Updated references
(4) Revised subsections 5.2, 5.3, 5.4, 11.4, and footnote 3. (5) Removed subsection 11.5.
